questions.q: A fruit seller sells $40\%$ of the oranges that he has along with $4$ more oranges to a customer. He then sells $25\%$ of the remaining oranges and $4$ more oranges to the second customer. He then sells $80\%$ of the now remaining oranges to a third customer and is still left with $4$ oranges. How many oranges did the fruit seller have initially?
questions.s: Dekh bhai, aise successive walo me hamesha ulta (bottom-to-top) chala kar. Last me $80\%$ bech diye toh bache $20\%$. Diya hai $20\% = 4$ oranges. Yani third customer ke aane se pehle $20$ oranges the. Second ne $25\%$ beche + 4 aur. Yani $(75\% \text{ of R1}) - 4 = 20 \implies 75\% = 24 \implies R1 = 32$. Pehle wale ne $40\%$ beche + 4. Yani $(60\% \text{ of Total}) - 4 = 32 \implies 60\% = 36 \implies Total = 60$.

questions.q: A is able to complete a task in 15 days, while B takes 20 days to finish the same task. If they collaborate and work together for 4 days, what fraction of the work will still remain?
questions.s:
Given:

A completes work in 15 days

B completes work in 20 days

They work together for 4 days

Calculations:

⇒ LCM of 15 and 20 = 60

⇒ Total Work = 60 units

⇒ Efficiency of A = 60 / 15 = 4 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of B = 60 / 20 = 3 units/day

⇒ Combined efficiency = 4 + 3 = 7 units/day

⇒ Work done in 4 days = 7 × 4 = 28 units

⇒ Work remaining = 60 − 28 = 32 units

⇒ Fraction remaining = 32 / 60

⇒ Fraction remaining = 8 / 15

∴ The fraction of work remaining is 8/15.

questions.q: A person has three iron bars whose lengths are 20, 30 and 40 metres, respectively. He wants to cut pieces of the same length from each of the three bars. What is the least number of total pieces if he cuts without any wastage?
questions.s:
Given:

Iron bars lengths: 20m, 30m, 40m

Formula use:

To find the least total pieces, find the Greatest Common Divisor (GCD) of lengths.

Calculation:

GCD of 20 and 30 ⇒ 10

GCD of 10 and 40 ⇒ 10

The optimal length for each piece to ensure no wastage and the minimum total pieces is 10 meters.

Total pieces:

From 20m bar ⇒ 20m / 10m = 2 pieces

From 30m bar ⇒ 30m / 10m = 3 pieces

From 40m bar ⇒ 40m / 10m = 4 pieces

Total pieces = 2 + 3 + 4 = 9 pieces

questions.q: What is the number of digits required for numbering a book with 428 pages?
questions.s:
Given:

Total number of pages = 428

Formula Used:

Total digits required = (Number of pages with 1 digit) + (Number of pages with 2 digits × 2) + (Number of pages with 3 digits × 3)

Calculation:

Pages with 1 digit: 1 to 9

Number of pages = 9

Digits required = 9

Pages with 2 digits: 10 to 99

Number of pages = 99 - 10 + 1

Number of pages = 90

Digits required = 90 × 2

Digits required = 180

Pages with 3 digits: 100 to 428

Number of pages = 428 - 100 + 1

Number of pages = 329

Digits required = 329 × 3

Digits required = 987

Total digits required = 9 + 180 + 987

⇒ Total digits required = 1176

The total number of digits required for numbering a book with 428 pages is 1176.

o: High-altitude origin / उच्च ऊंचाई वाला उद्गम
Lateral erosion in flat terrain  / समतल भूभाग में पार्श्व अपरदन (Lateral erosion)

questions.q: A circular pizza having a radius of 21 cm. If 75% of it is eaten, what is the area of pizza remaining?
questions.s:
Given:

Radius r = 21 cm

75% eaten

Formula used:

Area of circle = π × r2

Calculations:

⇒ Total area = (22 / 7) × 212

⇒ Total area = (22 / 7) × 441

⇒ Total area = 22 × 63

⇒ Total area = 1386 cm2

⇒ Remaining% = 100 − 75 = 25%

⇒ Remaining area = 1386 × 25 / 100

⇒ Remaining area = 346.5 cm2

∴ The area of pizza remaining is 346.5 cm2.

questions.q:
Which of the following objectives are part of the National Population Policy (NPP) 2000?

1. Providing free and compulsory education up to 14 years of age

2. Increasing fertility rate to ensure demographic dividend

3. Reducing infant mortality rate below 30 per 1000 live births

4. Promoting delayed marriage for girls
questions.s:
The correct answer is Only 1, 3 and 4 are correct.

Key Points

  • The National Population Policy (NPP) 2000 was formulated with the objective of stabilizing the population of India while ensuring sustainable development and improving the quality of life of its citizens.
  • One of the key goals of the policy is providing free and compulsory education up to 14 years of age, as outlined in the Directive Principles of State Policy under the Indian Constitution. This helps address population issues through better awareness and education.
  • The policy aims to reduce the infant mortality rate (IMR) below 30 per 1000 live births by improving healthcare services, immunization programs, and maternal health facilities.
  • Promoting delayed marriage for girls is another critical goal of the policy. Encouraging marriage at a later age not only helps in reducing fertility rates but also allows women to pursue education and professional opportunities.
  • The policy focuses on several other measures such as addressing unmet needs for contraception, improving maternal healthcare, and achieving population stabilization by 2045.

Additional Information

  • Incorrect Option: Increasing fertility rate to ensure demographic dividend
    • This is incorrect as the National Population Policy (NPP) 2000 focuses on reducing the fertility rate, not increasing it.
    • Reducing fertility rates helps to stabilize population growth and improve socioeconomic indicators.
    • Achieving a stable Total Fertility Rate (TFR) is one of the major goals of the policy, aiming for a replacement-level TFR of 2.1.
  • Importance of Infant Mortality Rate Reduction
    • Reducing the infant mortality rate (IMR) is a key indicator of healthcare quality in a country.
    • It reflects improvements in areas such as nutrition, immunization, sanitation, and access to healthcare services.

questions.q: For a rigid body, the angular velocity of any particle about a given axis of rotation is:
o: Proportional to its distance from the axis
Inversely proportional to its distance from the axis
questions.s:
The Correct answer is The same for all particles.

Key Points

  • In a rigid body, all particles are fixed relative to each other and move collectively during rotation.
  • The angular velocity is a measure of the rate of rotation of a body about a given axis and is denoted as ω (omega).
  • For a rigid body, the angular velocity of all particles is the same because they rotate together about the same axis at the same rate.
  • While the linear velocity of particles depends on their distance from the axis of rotation, the angular velocity remains constant for all particles of the rigid body.
  • This uniformity of angular velocity ensures that the body remains rigid and its shape does not change during rotation.
  • Angular velocity is a vector quantity, having both magnitude and direction, where the direction is determined by the right-hand rule.
  • The concept of angular velocity is widely used in mechanics, engineering, and physics to study rotational motion.

Additional Information

  • Proportional to its distance from the axis
    • The linear velocity of a particle in a rigid body is proportional to its distance from the axis of rotation. However, angular velocity is the same for all particles.
    • This is because linear velocity (v) is calculated as v = ω × r, where r is the distance from the axis, and ω is the angular velocity.
  • Inversely proportional to its distance from the axis
    • This statement is incorrect because angular velocity does not depend on the distance from the axis. However, other properties, like torque, can depend inversely on certain factors.
  • Always zero
    • For a rigid body in rotational motion, angular velocity is never zero unless the body is at rest.
    • If angular velocity were zero, the body would not exhibit any rotational motion.

questions.q:
A sentence is provided in indirect speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding direct speech.

He said that he would join the meeting after lunch.
o: "I will join the meeting after lunch," he said.
"I would join the meeting after lunch," he said.
"I shall join the meeting after lunch," he said.
"I can join the meeting after lunch," he said.
questions.s:
The correct answer is Option 1.
 
Key Points
  • Direct Speech: "I will join the meeting after lunch," he said.
  • Key Conversions:
    • "that he would join" becomes "I will join"
      • The reporting clause "he said that" is converted to "he said" and followed by the direct speech in quotes.
      • The pronoun "he" is changed to "I" to indicate the speaker's original words.
      • The verb "would" is changed to "will" to match the future tense in direct speech.
    • The time reference "after lunch" remains unchanged.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.
 
Additional Information
  • Option 2: "I would join the meeting after lunch," he said.
    • The use of "would" instead of "will" is incorrect in direct speech for this context.
  • Option 3: "I shall join the meeting after lunch," he said.
    • The use of "shall" is less common and would not typically be used in this context.
  • Option 4: "I can join the meeting after lunch," he said.
    • The use of "can" changes the meaning of the sentence and does not accurately reflect the original intent.

questions_hin.q_hi: Q18. What causes a river to develop meanders? / किसी नदी में विसर्प (meanders - घुमाव) विकसित होने का क्या कारण है? [SSC CGL Tier 1, 16 Sep 2025, Shift-2]
o_hi: High-altitude origin / उच्च ऊंचाई वाला उद्गम
Lateral erosion in flat terrain  / समतल भूभाग में पार्श्व अपरदन (Lateral erosion)
Sudden tectonic uplift / अचानक विवर्तनिक उत्थान
Ocean current influence / समुद्री धारा का प्रभाव
questions_hin.s_hi: Distinctive meanders (massive snake-like curves) robustly develop predominantly in the mature and old, slow stages of a major river's course, typically crossing highly flat terrain (plains). As the river's steep gradient drastically decreases, the water flows much slower and intense vertical down-cutting absolutely stops. Instead, the river dynamically begins to aggressively erode laterally (sideways) into its banks. / विशिष्ट विसर्प (बड़े पैमाने पर सांप जैसे घुमाव) मुख्य रूप से एक प्रमुख नदी के मार्ग के परिपक्व और पुराने, धीमे चरणों में मजबूती से विकसित होते हैं, आमतौर पर अत्यधिक समतल भूभाग (मैदानों) को पार करते हैं। जैसे-जैसे नदी का तीव्र ढाल काफी कम हो जाता है, पानी बहुत धीमी गति से बहता है और तीव्र ऊर्ध्वाधर डाउन-कटिंग बिल्कुल रुक जाती है। इसके बजाय, नदी गतिशील रूप से आक्रामक रूप से अपने किनारों में लंबवत (sideways) रूप से अपरदन (erode) करना शुरू कर देती है।

questions_hin.q_hi: A circular pizza having a radius of 21 cm. If 75% of it is eaten, what is the area of pizza remaining?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Given:

Radius r = 21 cm

75% eaten

Formula used:

Area of circle = π × r2

Calculations:

⇒ Total area = (22 / 7) × 212

⇒ Total area = (22 / 7) × 441

⇒ Total area = 22 × 63

⇒ Total area = 1386 cm2

⇒ Remaining% = 100 − 75 = 25%

⇒ Remaining area = 1386 × 25 / 100

⇒ Remaining area = 346.5 cm2

∴ The area of pizza remaining is 346.5 cm2.

questions_hin.q_hi:
Which of the following objectives are part of the National Population Policy (NPP) 2000?

1. Providing free and compulsory education up to 14 years of age

2. Increasing fertility rate to ensure demographic dividend

3. Reducing infant mortality rate below 30 per 1000 live births

4. Promoting delayed marriage for girls
questions_hin.s_hi:
The correct answer is Only 1, 3 and 4 are correct.

Key Points

  • The National Population Policy (NPP) 2000 was formulated with the objective of stabilizing the population of India while ensuring sustainable development and improving the quality of life of its citizens.
  • One of the key goals of the policy is providing free and compulsory education up to 14 years of age, as outlined in the Directive Principles of State Policy under the Indian Constitution. This helps address population issues through better awareness and education.
  • The policy aims to reduce the infant mortality rate (IMR) below 30 per 1000 live births by improving healthcare services, immunization programs, and maternal health facilities.
  • Promoting delayed marriage for girls is another critical goal of the policy. Encouraging marriage at a later age not only helps in reducing fertility rates but also allows women to pursue education and professional opportunities.
  • The policy focuses on several other measures such as addressing unmet needs for contraception, improving maternal healthcare, and achieving population stabilization by 2045.

Additional Information

  • Incorrect Option: Increasing fertility rate to ensure demographic dividend
    • This is incorrect as the National Population Policy (NPP) 2000 focuses on reducing the fertility rate, not increasing it.
    • Reducing fertility rates helps to stabilize population growth and improve socioeconomic indicators.
    • Achieving a stable Total Fertility Rate (TFR) is one of the major goals of the policy, aiming for a replacement-level TFR of 2.1.
  • Importance of Infant Mortality Rate Reduction
    • Reducing the infant mortality rate (IMR) is a key indicator of healthcare quality in a country.
    • It reflects improvements in areas such as nutrition, immunization, sanitation, and access to healthcare services.

questions_hin.q_hi: For a rigid body, the angular velocity of any particle about a given axis of rotation is:
o_hi: Proportional to its distance from the axis
Inversely proportional to its distance from the axis
questions_hin.s_hi:
The Correct answer is The same for all particles.

Key Points

  • In a rigid body, all particles are fixed relative to each other and move collectively during rotation.
  • The angular velocity is a measure of the rate of rotation of a body about a given axis and is denoted as ω (omega).
  • For a rigid body, the angular velocity of all particles is the same because they rotate together about the same axis at the same rate.
  • While the linear velocity of particles depends on their distance from the axis of rotation, the angular velocity remains constant for all particles of the rigid body.
  • This uniformity of angular velocity ensures that the body remains rigid and its shape does not change during rotation.
  • Angular velocity is a vector quantity, having both magnitude and direction, where the direction is determined by the right-hand rule.
  • The concept of angular velocity is widely used in mechanics, engineering, and physics to study rotational motion.

Additional Information

  • Proportional to its distance from the axis
    • The linear velocity of a particle in a rigid body is proportional to its distance from the axis of rotation. However, angular velocity is the same for all particles.
    • This is because linear velocity (v) is calculated as v = ω × r, where r is the distance from the axis, and ω is the angular velocity.
  • Inversely proportional to its distance from the axis
    • This statement is incorrect because angular velocity does not depend on the distance from the axis. However, other properties, like torque, can depend inversely on certain factors.
  • Always zero
    • For a rigid body in rotational motion, angular velocity is never zero unless the body is at rest.
    • If angular velocity were zero, the body would not exhibit any rotational motion.

questions_hin.q_hi:
A sentence is provided in indirect speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding direct speech.

He said that he would join the meeting after lunch.
o_hi: "I will join the meeting after lunch," he said.
"I would join the meeting after lunch," he said.
"I shall join the meeting after lunch," he said.
"I can join the meeting after lunch," he said.
questions_hin.s_hi:
The correct answer is Option 1.
 
Key Points
  • Direct Speech: "I will join the meeting after lunch," he said.
  • Key Conversions:
    • "that he would join" becomes "I will join"
      • The reporting clause "he said that" is converted to "he said" and followed by the direct speech in quotes.
      • The pronoun "he" is changed to "I" to indicate the speaker's original words.
      • The verb "would" is changed to "will" to match the future tense in direct speech.
    • The time reference "after lunch" remains unchanged.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.
 
Additional Information
  • Option 2: "I would join the meeting after lunch," he said.
    • The use of "would" instead of "will" is incorrect in direct speech for this context.
  • Option 3: "I shall join the meeting after lunch," he said.
    • The use of "shall" is less common and would not typically be used in this context.
  • Option 4: "I can join the meeting after lunch," he said.
    • The use of "can" changes the meaning of the sentence and does not accurately reflect the original intent.
